name: manual_2361b0
claim: When a CI dispatcher script sets a failure flag (FAIL=1) instead of exiting directly inside a branch, that branch's own failure path needs its own regression test -- a test that only exercises a sibling branch (e.g. a different scanner's direct-exit path) does not prove the flag-setting branch actually propagates to the script's final exit code
conditions: CI dispatcher FAIL flag branch coverage
test only one branch of shared exit code

decisions.notes: CodeRabbit review #4983422918 on orama-system PR #321: scripts/ci/test_run_agent_security_scans.sh had one regression test for the aguara branch's failure propagation (a stub binary that exits 1 directly), but scan_ramparts()'s GITHUB_ACTIONS-set/tool-unavailable branch sets FAIL=1 and falls through rather than exiting immediately -- a regression that dropped that assignment could still pass the existing suite. Added a second assertion (GITHUB_ACTIONS=1, PATH restricted to /usr/bin:/bin so ramparts/cargo aren't found, expect exit 1) that specifically exercises the flag-setting branch. Confirmed the finding against current code first (grepped scan_ramparts()'s actual FAIL=1 site) before writing the test, per this session's verify-against-current-code discipline.
